decision.summaryForCoordinator: As with FX-7, the FX-8 predecessor was never independently reviewed, so nothing here was already verified and the subject's claim about v1 was the first thing to measure. It is exact: v1's fx8Intent is 211 characters against live's 372, v1 != live, and live.startswith(v1) is TRUE, so '211-of-372 true prefix' holds on every element including the milder true-prefix characterisation. What makes this one pointed is WHICH 161 characters v1 had dropped: 'Running only the first half would produce a passing test that reads as confinement evidence, which is the failure mode this whole artifact is organized against.' That is precisely the sentence warning against the thing this dispatch prohibits, so v1's truncation had removed the source warning for the very failure mode I was asked to police. v2 restores it — fx8Intent == live at 372 against 372 — and adds fx8Proves == live, whose value itself ends 'and the class is INVALID if only the first half is run'. I read every occurrence of 'confinement' in context rather than counting, since the word necessarily returns with the restored sentence: five occurrences, one being the restored warning and four being negations, with 'confined', 'proves confinement', 'isolation' and 'sandbox' all at zero. Structurally the brokered state asserts PR-5, a refusal family, and fx8Proves attributes ENFORCEMENT to that half in v9's own word, which is not confinement. The both-halves attack fails three ways: two structural booleans, v9's 'Both assertions are mandatory' inside the restored intent, and the invalidity clause inside proves — with the token 'optional' occurring zero times. One nuance from the diff is worth your attention because it makes the v1 defect milder than it first reads: v1 ALREADY carried bothHalvesMandatory and invalidIfOnlyBrokeredHalfRun, so the structural guard predates the repair. v1 was never at risk of making the second half optional; what it had lost was v9's explanation of why the guard exists. The repair restores the rationale, not the rule. The diff is otherwise surgical — zero paths removed, five added, six changed of which four are identity or prose, and every /initialStates path byte-identical. I also verified the one substantive sibling claim: the role says FX-8 'reuses the disclosure-of-absence-of-enforcement posture, not FX-2B bytes', and live v9's FX-2B proves reads 'DISCLOSURE (and it proves the ABSENCE of enforcement, deliberately)', so the attribution is exact, while the token FX-2B occurs once in the whole subject and no FX-2B bytes are reproduced. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at 698ed107 and 0444 at both samplings, v1 unmoved at cb6db222 and 0444, six of six cited digests equal live bytes, both cited standings confirmed at Claude ACCEPT 0/0 with no Codex verdict anywhere in this family, the D-163 join confirms OBL-FX-AUTHORING still leftoverDesign true with owner none and FX-8 inside its fourteen, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, bare integers only 0/2/26, no control bytes, SATISFIED and QUALIFIED at zero. Seventeen attacks run, seventeen refuted, zero findings. Two things to note rather than fix, both shared with FX-7 v2: the lands array carries a defect-class string rather than a finding id, which is honest given that no FX-8 finding exists; and FX-8 v1 has no verdict of any kind, so a later citation of 'FX-8 v1 reviewed' would be false on the current bytes.
